name: Global L10N Master 9-Gate & Profile Audit
note: This validator once required the false privacy claim: the shared spec pinned the lie in place rather than catching it. It also spent a long time requiring screens.stats.tabs.stats and .achievements — the names the stats screen carried before it was rewritten — which is the only reason those two keys survived in thirteen languages. A profile can be as stale as the code it checks, so it gets mutated like anything else.

mutations.name: a language loses a key the others have
mutations.why: The key falls back to its raw identifier, so one locale shows `modals.dailyReward.desc` where the others show a sentence.

mutations.name: the first stats tab label goes missing
mutations.why: The profile's required-key check was pointed at a dead key for so long that nothing noticed. Repointing it at achievements.statsTab is worthless unless the check actually fires when the key is gone.

mutations.name: a stats tab label grows past the segmented button
mutations.why: The length rule read a key with no fallback, so `typeof statTab === 'string'` was false and fourteen characters had not been enforced in a long time. Three tabs share one row; a long label pushes the other two off it. The first attempt used a 13-character string against a limit of 14, so it passed and was right to.

mutations.name: Japanese noun and verb clauses are joined with ya
mutations.why: J-01 must fail for the grammar regression, without prescribing one exact acceptable rewrite.
mutations.find: ゲームオーバーになったり、途中でやめたりすると、
mutations.replace: ゲームオーバーや途中でやめると
mutations.expectFailure: JA parallel clauses mix a noun and a verb (J-01)

mutations.name: a translation grows a token its source never had
mutations.why: External audit V08: the token gate skipped every key whose source had no tokens, so "Start {ghost}" against a plain "시작" counted as symmetric. The player would see the braces, or a value that never arrives. It first survived even with the gate fixed: the engine never loaded keypad.* at all — it read only the section of common.js named after the file, 70 of 465 strings per language. The loader now reads every section; this mutation holds both fixes.

mutations.name: a French colon goes back to a plain space
mutations.why: Gemini FR-07 (2026-10-13): 95 French UI strings had a plain space before : ; ! ?, so a narrow button could break the line there and leave the colon alone at the start of the next line. Gate 10 asks for a no-break space.

mutations.name: a straight apostrophe comes back in French
mutations.why: Gemini FR-26: the newer French files (replay.js) still had programmer's apostrophes while the rest used ’. Gate 10 refuses ' in French.

mutations.name: French loading text goes back to three dots
mutations.why: Gemini FR-29 (2026-10-14): four French loading texts used "..." while three others used the ellipsis; gate 10 rule 6 asks for … everywhere in French.
